reasoning_note: FTP outbound from clinical subnet at 2am is unusual but could be a scheduled backup misconfiguration
Billing user accessing 47 records late at night is a bit high but could be end-of-month reconciliation
Cross-VLAN SMB from admin to medical device subnet is odd but admin staff sometimes troubleshoot devices
340MB SFTP from lab server to external IP during business hours needs verification with lab manager
Infusion pump hitting external HTTPS is probably a firmware update check or vendor cloud sync
High DNS volume from a medical device is probably just chatty network stack, devices do weird things
Float nurse working overnight across departments would explain multi-dept access at 2:30am
ICMP sweep from management VLAN during business hours is likely someone running a network scan for inventory
RDP to device subnet on Saturday morning is probably IT doing weekend maintenance
Large PACS transfer could be a teleradiology feed or image sharing with another facility
Another PACS outbound transfer at 4am, likely scheduled replication or offsite backup
Proprietary wireless from IoT device to unknown destination is strange but could be a Bluetooth peripheral pairing
Service account pulling 312 records across all departments at 1am is suspicious even if it is a reporting job
Telnet from a ventilator to the gateway is unusual but older devices sometimes use telnet for management traffic
EHR to backup server over SMB at 2:30pm is clearly a scheduled backup job
Pharmacy HTTPS outbound on Saturday is probably automated drug database or inventory sync
Patient monitor traffic spike at 3am is likely a noisy sensor or device restart cycling
EHR server scanning all internal subnets on common exploit ports at 3am is textbook compromised host behavior
Physician accessing 22 records via VPN in the evening is normal remote charting
1.1GB exfiltrated from a nurse station in 3 minutes to an external IP is highly suspicious

q21_note: These alerts are pure network data with IPs and protocols, a nurse or physician would have no way to connect them to specific patients or safety risks.
q22_note: The raw IDS data supports network-level decisions but lacks business context like asset ownership and data classification that management would want before approving costly actions.
